 Home Feature Story TV Buying a TV for GTA 6? Beware of these 5 marketing claims
 By Vikhyat Rishi | Updated on 09-Nov-2026 Add Digit as a 
preferred source Follow Us With GTA 6 just days away, a new TV starts to look tempting. Spec sheets promise 8K, 120Hz, HDR 1000 and AI picture modes. A 120Hz screen can be great for games that support it, but that spec alone doesn’t tell us whether GTA 6 will. 
 Rockstar has confirmed the console platforms and release date, but hasn’t announced the game’s resolution or frame-rate target. So those numbers alone can’t tell you whether an upgrade is worth it. 
 Until launch, there’s plenty of room for speculation and plenty of sales pitches.
 1. You need an 8K TV to get the full experience
 There’s no published Rockstar requirement for an 8K television. The game is confirmed for current PlayStation and Xbox consoles; that doesn’t mean it will render at 8K, or that an 8K screen will reveal extra detail from it.
 Also read: Getting a new TV for GTA 6? These 5 OLED TVs are just right for your PS5 
 Some PS5 models support 8K output for games that support 8K, but that is a capability of the console, not a promise about GTA 6. For most buyers, a good 4K TV is the sensible starting point. Spend extra for 8K only if you have other reasons to want it.
 2. A 120Hz TV means GTA 6 will run at 120 frames per second
 A TV’s refresh rate tells you how often its screen can update. It doesn’t dictate how many frames a game will produce. PlayStation says 120Hz output works with games that support a 120Hz frame rate; Xbox likewise makes higher frame rates an option for developers. Rockstar hasn’t announced GTA 6’s frame-rate target.
 A 120Hz set can still be useful for other games that support higher frame rates. Just don’t buy one on the assumption that this game will use every one of those updates.
 3. HDMI 2.1 means every port has every gaming feature
 Look past the badge and check the TV’s manual. PlayStation says that even TVs with HDMI 2.1 may not support ALLM, or Auto Low Latency Mode. Xbox advises checking which ports on a TV support its advanced features; some sets offer them only on specific inputs.
 Before buying, confirm that the port you plan to use supports the features you care about such as 4K at 120Hz, VRR and ALLM. Count how many compatible ports you need if you’ll connect more than one console or a sound system.
 4. HDR 1000 means spectacular HDR
 A peak-brightness number is only one part of an HDR picture. It doesn’t tell you, by itself, how well a TV handles dark detail, color, contrast or bright highlights across a scene. A useful reminder comes from VESA’s DisplayHDR testing framework, which assesses several aspects of display performance, including luminance, color, contrast and black levels. A format badge or a single number can’t tell the whole story.
 When comparing TVs, look for credible hands-on measurements and pay attention to the room where you’ll play. A bright room puts different demands on a screen than a dark one. And whatever the set’s label says, plan to run the console’s HDR setup and adjust the TV’s picture to suit your space.
 5. AI picture enhancement always makes games look better
 “AI” sounds like an automatic upgrade, but picture processing is a matter of taste and it can sometimes get in the way. Rockstar’s own HDR troubleshooting guide suggests switching off picture-enhancement features, including AI, Smart, Dynamic or Adaptive settings, when diagnosing display problems. It also recommends trying Game Mode. That’s troubleshooting advice, not a claim that every enhancement is bad. 
 Start with Game Mode and the console’s HDR calibration. Then try extra processing one setting at a time. Keep it if you prefer the picture and it doesn’t interfere with responsiveness.
 What TV specs can improve your GTA 6 experience?
 A 4K TV with low input lag, good real-world contrast and HDR performance, plus VRR and ALLM, is a more useful shortlist than a wall of buzzwords. If you want 4K at 120Hz for other supported games, verify that the TV and the specific HDMI port both support it.
 Most of all, buy for the games you play and the room you have. GTA 6 may look extraordinary but until Rockstar publishes its display specifications, a TV that promises the perfect GTA 6 experience is selling you a guess.
